shifts.branch_range: near path if |replacement_runtime - site_runtime| >> 2 < 0x1ffffff (rflib 0x1a218c/0x1a2194), i.e. |delta| < 128 MiB
shifts.trampoline_arena: libRFLib.so .bss 0x4e2000 + counter*200, counter at 0x4e0238, capped at 0x100 (rflib 0x1a2bd0-0x1a2be0)

near_4_bytes.note: overwrites 1 instruction; the displaced copy goes to the trampoline

far_20_bytes.note: nop; ldr x17,[site+12]; br x17; .quad replacement.  The mod displaces 4 or 5 instructions (4 if (site+8)%8==0 else 5) and resumes at site+20 (rflib 0x1a2198-0x1a21a8, 0x1a22e0-0x1a2338, constant at 0x121388)

unresolved.why: 289 of the 290 sites are the exact start of a function in libPVZ2.so's .eh_frame FDE table; this one has no FDE.  It is still a function entry (the word before it is a 'ret' and the site itself is the prologue 'stp x29, x30, [sp, #-0x80]!'), but it carries no unwind information, so the extent of the function it hooks cannot be delimited from the tables.

A64HookFunction was called with a NULL backup pointer for these, so the engine took the path at rflib 0x1a21e0 -> 0x1a227c and wrote the branch over the first instruction without copying it anywhere.  The bytes are in orig_bytes, but whether the mod's replacement reproduces their effect is not decidable from the log: the replacement code lives in libRFLib.so and is not part of these inputs.

the displaced instruction is PC-relative (adrp), so the engine turned it into ldr xN,[pc+8] + a literal (rflib 0x1a2a1c-0x1a2a38).  The literal is an absolute address of the target layout and has to be re-emitted for the port; the trampoline_bytes below are the oracle run's bytes, not the port's.

the 287 distinct replacements are internal functions of libRFLib.so (which exports 12 symbols, none of them these).  The port has to supply its own implementation for each; this table only fixes which libPVZ2 function each one replaces.
